about.title: Vallejo Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Vallejo is home to more than 121,000 people, and most of them will sit in a waiting room, fill a prescription, or check into a Solano County hospital at some point. The overwhelming majority of those visits go the way they should. Some do not. A medical malpractice claim asks a narrow question: did a provider fail to act as a reasonably careful professional would have in the same situation, and did that failure cause real harm? A disappointing result by itself is not enough. That distinction matters, because California's MICRA rules make these cases technical from the very first step. There is typically one year from the date you discovered the harm to act, and never more than three years from the injury itself. A 90-day written notice must go to the provider before a lawsuit is filed. Non-economic damages are capped by statute, though the cap increases annually. And a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the records and support the claim. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Vallejo patients and families with an independent attorney who can evaluate whether those pieces line up.

items.title: The clock is shorter than most people expect
items.desc: MICRA generally gives one year from discovery and never more than three years from the injury, and a 90-day notice has to reach the provider before suit. Connecting early with an independent attorney helps keep those windows open.

items.title: An honest read on whether it was malpractice
items.desc: A bad outcome alone is not a claim under California law. The attorney you're connected with can arrange the qualified medical expert review that is almost always required before a case can move forward.

items.question: I was treated at a Vallejo emergency room after a car crash on I-80. Can I have a malpractice claim on top of the crash claim?
items.answer: It is possible for two separate claims to arise from one event. The crash claim concerns the driver who caused the collision, while a malpractice claim would concern whether the hospital or its staff met the standard of care afterward. Vallejo recorded 439 injury collisions in 2025, so this situation is not unusual, but each claim has its own deadlines and proof requirements. An independent attorney can look at both together.

items.question: How do I know if what happened to me was actually malpractice?
items.answer: Under California law, a poor result is not malpractice by itself. The question is whether the provider did something a reasonably careful provider would not have done, or failed to do something they should have, and whether that caused harm. Answering that almost always requires a qualified medical expert to review the records. That review is one of the first things the attorney you're connected with will consider.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a Solano County malpractice case?
items.answer: California's MICRA law caps non-economic damages such as pain and suffering, and that cap rises each year. Economic losses like medical costs and lost income are treated differently. No one can tell you in advance what a case is worth, and LawProactive never makes those predictions. An independent attorney can explain how the current figures apply to your circumstances.
